author: Matilda Carpenter Sun Staff Writer
title: Tech Time with Tilly: Dumb phones - a smart choice? | News | yumasun.com
text:
There has been an interesting trend lately that has been bucking the traditional trajectory of tech sales: the return of the dumb phone. In an era of subscription fatigue, constant ads and apps that are designed to keep you glued to the screen, it makes sense that more people are ditching the $1,000+ smart phones and opting for something that is scaled down to the essentials of what a phone can do. But what kind of tradeoffs have to be managed to take a step back in time?
As someone who periodically enjoys a good “tech detox” now and again, I have personally oscillated between a smart phone and my 10-year-old, incredibly basic flip phone. The first thing I usually notice (after a “withdrawal” period), is that I feel incredibly productive, in spite of no longer carrying a Library of Alexandria in my pocket. It is easier to sit down and complete my tasks without those pesty notifications from apps and the allure of just one more TikTok. I read more, do more chores around the house, and I even manage to squeeze in time for simple relaxation, sans the constant dopamine fix of social media apps.
